name: ayywi
description: Lightweight, framework-agnostic, AI-first design system. One CSS class contract for HTML, Vue, Svelte, Angular, server templates — plus typed React components.

entrypoints.ayywi/css: Full stylesheet (tokens + base + all components) in cascade layers ayywi.tokens < ayywi.base < ayywi.components < ayywi.brand — any unlayered app CSS wins. ayywi/ayywi.min.css is the minified file.
entrypoints.ayywi/ayywi.unlayered.css: Same without cascade layers. Use it when an unlayered CSS reset (Tailwind v3 preflight, normalize.css) would otherwise override components.
entrypoints.ayywi/css/<file>.css: Per-file layered CSS: tokens.css, base.css, then one file per component (button.css, card.css…).
entrypoints.ayywi/fonts.css: Self-hosted brand fonts (Sora, Unbounded, Caveat; woff2, unicode-range subsets). ayywi/fonts-google.css loads them from Google instead.
entrypoints.ayywi: Framework-free JS: tokens, class helpers (buttonClass…), controllers (connectPopover, connectMenu, enhanceTooltip), toast(), iconSvg(), setTheme/setDensity/setBrand, cssVar(). Server-safe.
entrypoints.ayywi/react: React components (re-exports everything from ayywi). Marked "use client".
entrypoints.ayywi/elements: Custom elements for any framework or plain HTML: <ayy-menu>, <ayy-theme-toggle>, <ayy-toc>, <ayy-tabs>, <ayy-carousel>, <ayy-dialog>, <ayy-popover>, <ayy-tooltip>, plus the card spotlight. dist/elements.global.js registers them from a <script> and exposes window.ayywi (toast, setTheme, setDensity, setBrand).
entrypoints.ayywi/tokens.json: DTCG-style token source ($value = dark, extensions hold light/density). Extra themes are defined in tokens/themes/*.json.
entrypoints.ayywi/tokens/<file>: Exports for other platforms: dark.json, light.json, dark-soft.json, light-gray.json, density/*.json (plain DTCG, for Style Dictionary / Figma), ayywi.scss, Ayywi.swift (SwiftUI), Ayywi.kt (Jetpack Compose).
entrypoints.npx ayywi: CLI: `lint` (checks app code against this manifest), `init` (sets up AI agent files + MCP), `mcp` (MCP server over stdio).

conventions.naming: BEM: .ayy-block, .ayy-block__element, .ayy-block--modifier. Modifiers combine: class="ayy-button ayy-button--outline ayy-button--sm".
conventions.state: State lives in native/ARIA attributes (disabled, :checked, aria-selected, aria-invalid, [open], :popover-open) so every framework drives it the same way.
conventions.theming: No attribute = follow OS (dark or light). data-theme="dark" | "light" | "dark-soft" | "light-gray" forces a theme on any element and its subtree (.dark/.light classes work too). See "themes" for what each one does; every theme keeps text at WCAG AA. setTheme() switches and persists; getColorScheme() says "dark" or "light".
conventions.density: Controls default to compact (touch on touch-first devices). data-density="compact" | "comfortable" | "touch" on any element resizes buttons, inputs, tabs, switches, checkboxes and menu items below it.
conventions.brands: Semantic tokens can be overridden per brand: load ayywi/brands/<name>.css and set data-brand. Components never change.
conventions.direction: All layout uses logical properties; set dir="rtl" on any ancestor and components mirror. Icons that point along the reading direction (arrows) need directional (ayy-icon--directional) to mirror too.
conventions.elements: Custom elements are light DOM (no shadow root): write the same ayy- markup inside them; they add behaviour. Vue: compilerOptions.isCustomElement = (t) => t.startsWith("ayy-"); Angular: CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA.
conventions.highContrast: Every stateful component has a forced-colors (Windows High Contrast) style using system colours.
conventions.icons: Hugeicons is the icon library: install @hugeicons/core-free-icons (an optional peer; ayywi renders its data, so there's still no runtime dependency). React: <Icon icon={Search01Icon} />. Elsewhere: iconSvg(Search01Icon), or the SVG pasted from hugeicons.com with class="ayy-icon" and no fixed colour attributes. Icons use currentColor and 1.25em (the text size); size sm/md/lg/xl is 16/20/24/32px (--ayy-size-icon-*).

rules: Use existing ayywi classes/components and their variants before writing any custom CSS. Never add a second UI kit.
Never hardcode colours (hex, rgb, hsl, named). Use var(--ayy-color-*) tokens; for tints use color-mix(in srgb, var(--ayy-color-text) N%, transparent) or the wash/line tokens.
Use logical properties only: margin-inline-start, padding-inline, inset-inline-end, text-align: start. Never left/right/margin-left/padding-right, so RTL works.

Spacing, radius, font size, shadows and motion come from tokens (--ayy-space-*, --ayy-radius-*, --ayy-text-*, --ayy-control-*, --ayy-shadow-*, --ayy-ease-*, --ayy-duration-*). Control sizes follow data-density — don't hardcode heights.

Theme with data-theme="dark|light|dark-soft|light-gray" (or nothing = follow OS). Never write separate dark-mode colours; tokens already switch. Rebrand by overriding semantic tokens or loading a brand file, not by restyling components.

Every interactive element keeps its visible :focus-visible ring. Icon-only buttons need aria-label. Form controls need a label. State lives in native/ARIA attributes (disabled, checked, aria-selected, aria-invalid, open).
Stateful styles need a @media (forced-colors: active) fallback (Windows High Contrast erases fills).

Prefer animating transform and opacity (use a logical property like inset-inline-start only when the motion must follow text direction). Everything must still work under prefers-reduced-motion — base.css collapses ayy animations. Scroll-in motion comes from .ayy-reveal, not a script; nothing loops unless it shows a live state.

The frame is monochrome; colour comes from the content. Set --ayy-spot (to an --ayy-accent-* token) on the card, section or page that shows the content, and the spotlight, contents bar, section numbers, icon tiles and .ayy-accent-text inside pick it up. Never tint the navbar, buttons or page background per page.

Pages follow one anatomy: .ayy-skip-link, Navbar, then <main> made of .ayy-section blocks at .ayy-container width (fading Separators between marketing sections), then the footer. One call to action per view: a ring (marketing) or primary (app) button; everything else outline or ghost.
Every gets width and height (its real size) so nothing jumps while it loads. Product screenshots go in a Frame. Draw small product visuals as SVG with tokens instead of images with text baked in.
No :dir() selectors — minifiers rewrite them into :lang() lists that ignore dir="rtl". Logical properties make direction checks unnecessary.
Body text must fall back to system fonts — never remove the system-ui stack from --ayy-font-body (CJK/Arabic/Cyrillic rely on it).

Icons come from Hugeicons (@hugeicons/core-free-icons): <Icon icon={Search01Icon} /> in React, iconSvg(Search01Icon) or the pasted SVG with class="ayy-icon" elsewhere. Don't add another icon set. Icons are decorative (aria-hidden) unless you give them a label.

In React import from "ayywi/react"; in other frameworks and plain HTML use the class names, the class helpers from "ayywi" (buttonClass…) and the custom elements from "ayywi/elements" (<ayy-tabs>, <ayy-dialog>, <ayy-menu>, <ayy-popover>, <ayy-tooltip>, <ayy-toc>, <ayy-carousel>, <ayy-theme-toggle>).
Run `npx ayywi lint` after UI changes and fix every error it reports.

attributes.data-theme: "dark" | "light" | "dark-soft" | "light-gray" — force a theme on this element and its subtree. None = follow the OS (dark or light). dark-soft lowers the contrast (charcoal instead of black); light-gray puts white cards and panels on a grey page.
attributes.data-density: "compact" | "comfortable" | "touch" — control sizes for this subtree. None = compact, or touch on touch-first devices.

components.name: Button
components.description: Triggers an action. Pill-shaped, monochrome primary with a subtle lift on hover.
whenToUse: Any action the user can take: submit, open, save, delete.
Links that should look like actions (apply buttonClass() to the <a>).
whenNotToUse: Navigation inside running text — use a plain link.
Toggling a setting on/off — use Switch.

classes.ayy-button: Root. Alone it is the primary button.
classes.ayy-button--secondary: Quiet filled button for secondary actions.
classes.ayy-button--outline: Bordered, transparent. Neutral alternative to secondary.
classes.ayy-button--ghost: No border or fill until hover. Toolbars, icon buttons.
classes.ayy-button--ring: Showcase call to action: quiet fill inside a gradient ring that spins on hover and focus. For marketing and portfolio pages; one per view.

components.js: buttonClass({ variant?, size?, className? }) → string
a11y: Icon-only buttons need aria-label.
Use disabled on <button>; on <a> use aria-disabled="true" (the class handles both).

On a marketing or portfolio page, the one call to action can be ring instead of primary, with an outline button beside it.
Put the icon (<Icon> or an .ayy-icon <svg>) before the label; the button sizes it (1.25em).

Don't use destructive for non-destructive emphasis.

components.name: Theme toggle
components.description: An icon button that switches between a dark and a light theme and remembers the choice. The moon or sun shows from CSS alone, following the colour scheme, so it's right on first paint.
whenToUse: A site or app header where readers pick light or dark.
whenNotToUse: Choosing between more than two themes, or "system" — use a Select or radio group with setTheme().
Theming one section — set data-theme on it.

classes.ayy-theme-toggle: On the button (with ayy-button ayy-button--outline ayy-button--icon). Stacks the two icons.

events.ayy-value-change: { value: string } — the theme just applied

components.name: App shell
components.description: The frame of a web app: a fixed-width sidebar (brand, navigation, footer) beside a main area, filling the viewport. The two scroll independently; on phones the sidebar stacks above the content as a single row that scrolls sideways.
whenToUse: The outer layout of a signed-in app or dashboard: a persistent list of destinations next to the page content.
Anything with five or more top-level destinations that should stay one click away.
whenNotToUse: A marketing site or a content page — use Navbar and Sections.
Switching views of one object inside a page — use Tabs.

components.name: Frame
components.description: A browser window around a screenshot, video or coded mock-up: a bar with three dots and an optional address, and a long soft shadow.
whenToUse: Showing product screens in a case study, landing page or portfolio card, so they read as product and not decoration.
whenNotToUse: Photos and illustrations — they don't need a window.
Live, interactive UI inside an app.

components.name: Chat
components.description: A conversation: incoming bubbles at the start edge, the reader's own inverted at the end, a typing indicator and quick-reply buttons.
whenToUse: AI assistants and agents.
Support or feedback widgets.
A scripted "say hi" section on a marketing page that hands off to email or LinkedIn.
whenNotToUse: Comments and threads on a document — use a list of cards.
Toast-style status messages — use Toast.

classes.ayy-chat: Root. role="log" when messages arrive live, so they're announced.
classes.ayy-chat__message: One message row: an optional avatar and its bubble.
classes.ayy-chat__message--out: Sent by the reader: end edge, primary colours.
classes.ayy-chat__bubble: The bubble. The corner by the avatar is squared off.
classes.ayy-chat__typing: Three pulsing dots inside a bubble while a reply is written. Give it role="img" and an aria-label.
classes.ayy-chat__replies: Quick replies under the conversation: small outline buttons, at the end edge.

a11y: Use role="log" on the conversation when messages arrive while the reader watches; they're announced politely, in order.
The typing dots are an image with a name ("Dani is typing"); remove the element when the message lands.
Quick replies are real buttons; after one is chosen, move focus to the next sensible place, not back to the top.
do: Keep bubbles short; split long answers into several messages.
Pair incoming messages with the sender's avatar the first time.
dont: Don't auto-scroll the page while someone is reading above.
Don't use colour alone to tell who's speaking; the side and avatar do it too.

components.name: Table
components.description: Data table with quiet hairlines, uppercase headers and hover rows. Styles plain table elements under .ayy-table.
whenToUse: Comparing items across the same attributes (projects × status × builds).
whenNotToUse: Layout — never use tables for layout.
Lists with one attribute — use a list.

classes.ayy-table-wrap: Scroll container around the table (horizontal overflow).
classes.ayy-table__num: On th/td with numbers: end-aligned, tabular digits.

react.import: import { Table, TableHeader, TableBody, TableFooter, TableRow, TableHead, TableCell, TableCaption } from "ayywi/react";

a11y: Use real <th> header cells with scope (React sets scope="col").
A <caption> or aria-label names the table for screen readers.
do: End-align numbers with numeric/ayy-table__num.
Keep cell content short; truncate with a tooltip if needed.
dont: Don't zebra-stripe; hairlines + hover are enough.
Don't nest interactive controls in every cell — one action column is plenty.
